title.zh: 卷一百二十四 列傳第十一: 塔本 哈剌亦哈赤北魯 塔塔統阿 岳璘帖穆爾 李楨 速哥 忙哥撒兒 孟速思
title.en: Volume 124 Biographies 11: Taben, Halayihachibeilu, Tatatonga, Yuelintiemuer, Lizhen, Suge, Manggesaer, Mengsusi
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 列傳第十一: 塔本 哈剌亦哈赤北魯 塔塔統阿 岳璘帖穆爾 李楨 速哥 忙哥撒兒 孟速思 Volume 124 Biographies 11: Taben, Halayihachibeilu, Tatatonga, Yuelintiemuer, Lizhen, Suge, Manggesaer, Mengsusi

sentences.zh: 塔本，伊吾廬人。

translations.literal: Taben was a man of Iwu Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Taben was a native of Iwu Lu.

sentences.zh: 人以其好揚人善，稱之曰揚公。

translations.literal: Because he was fond of praising others' good points, people called him Lord Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Because he delighted in commending others' virtues, people called him Lord Yang—the "Promoter."

sentences.zh: 父宋五設托陀，托陀者，其國主所賜號，猶華言國老也。

translations.literal: His father was Song Wushe Tuotuo; Tuotuo was a title bestowed by the ruler of their state, equivalent in Chinese to guolao (elder of the state).
translations.idiomatic: His father was Song Wushe Tuotuo; tuotuo was a title granted by their ruler, corresponding to the Chinese office of guolao, elder statesman of the realm.

sentences.zh: 塔本初從太祖討諸部，屢厄艱危。

translations.literal: Taben first followed Taizu in campaigns against the various tribes, repeatedly meeting with grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: Taben first followed Taizu in the subjugation of the tribes, and time and again found himself in mortal danger.

sentences.zh: 復從圍燕，征遼西，下平灤、白霫諸城。

translations.literal: He again followed in the siege of Yan, the campaign in Liaoxi, and the capture of Pingluan, Baihui, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: He served again in the siege of Yan, the Liaodong campaign, and the reduction of Pingluan, Baihui, and the other towns.

sentences.zh: 軍士有妄殺人者，塔本戒之曰：「國之本，民也。

translations.literal: When soldiers wantonly killed people, Taben admonished them, saying: "The foundation of a state is its people.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers killed civilians without cause, Taben warned them: "A state rests upon its people.

sentences.zh: 殺人得地，何益於國。

translations.literal: To kill people and gain land—what benefit is there to the state?
translations.idiomatic: What good does it do the realm to win land by slaughtering the populace?

sentences.zh: 且殺無罪以堅敵心，非上意。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to kill the innocent and thereby harden the enemy's resolve is not the sovereign's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, executing the innocent only steels the enemy's will—and that is not what our lord intends."

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而喜之，賜金虎符，俾鎮撫白霫諸郡，號行省都元帥，管內得承制除縣吏，死囚得專決。

translations.literal: Taizu heard this and was pleased; he bestowed a gold tiger tally, appointed him to pacify the Baihui commanderies, and styled him Branch Secretariat Grand Marshal. Within his jurisdiction he could appoint county officials by imperial commission and decide capital cases on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu heard this he was delighted. He granted Taben a gold tiger tally and charged him with pacifying the Baihui districts, with the title Grand Marshal of the Branch Secretariat. Within his jurisdiction he could appoint county officials on his own authority and pass final judgment on capital cases.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙治興平。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to administer Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: In time his seat of government was moved to Xingping.

sentences.zh: 興平兵火傷殘，民慘無生意。

translations.literal: Xingping had been ravaged by war; the people were wretched and without means of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Xingping lay in ruins from war, and the people were so destitute they could scarcely keep body and soul together.

sentences.zh: 塔本召父老問所苦，為除之，薄賦斂，役有時。

translations.literal: Taben summoned the elders to ask what afflicted them, removed those burdens, lightened taxes and levies, and set corvée labor on a fixed schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Taben called the village elders to learn their grievances, lifted them where he could, reduced taxes and levies, and regulated labor service so it came only at proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 民大悅，乃相與告教，無違約束，歸者四集。

translations.literal: The people were greatly pleased; they exhorted one another to observe the regulations without breach, and returnees gathered from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced, urged one another to keep the rules, and refugees streamed back from every direction.

sentences.zh: 塔本始至，戶止七百，不一二年，乃至萬戶。

translations.literal: When Taben first arrived there were only seven hundred households; within a year or two the number reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Taben first arrived the register showed only seven hundred households; within a year or two there were ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 出己馬以寬驛人；

translations.literal: He provided his own horses to ease the burden on relay couriers;
translations.idiomatic: He supplied his own horses to spare the relay couriers;

sentences.zh: 貸廉吏銀，其子錢不能償者，焚其券。

translations.literal: he lent silver to honest officials, and when their sons could not repay the money he burned the promissory notes.
translations.idiomatic: lent silver to upright officials, and when their heirs could not repay the debt he burned the notes.

sentences.zh: 農不克耕，亦與之牛，比歲告稔，民用以饒。

translations.literal: When farmers could not till the fields he also gave them oxen; year after year they reported good harvests, and the people's livelihood grew ample.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers who lacked oxen to plow received cattle from him as well; harvest after harvest was reported bountiful, and the people grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔益中山、平定、平原隸行省。

translations.literal: In the gengyin year an edict added Zhongshan, Pingding, and Pingyuan to the branch secretariat's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year an edict placed Zhongshan, Pingding, and Pingyuan under the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甲午，盜李仙、越小哥等作亂，塔本止誅首惡，宥其詿誤。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year the bandits Li Xian, Yue Xiaoge, and others rose in revolt; Taben executed only the ringleaders and pardoned those who had been misled.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year bandits led by Li Xian and Yue Xiaoge rebelled; Taben put only the chief culprits to death and pardoned those drawn in by mistake.

sentences.zh: 癸卯立春日，宴群僚，歸而疾作，遂卒。

translations.literal: On the First Day of Spring in the guimao year he feasted his subordinates; upon returning he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the First Day of Spring in the guimao year he entertained his officials; he fell ill after returning home and died.

sentences.zh: 是夕星隕，隱隱有聲。

translations.literal: That evening a star fell, and a faint sound was heard.
translations.idiomatic: That night a star fell, accompanied by a low rumble.

sentences.zh: 遺命葬以紙衣瓦棺。

translations.literal: He left instructions to be buried in paper garments and a tile coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He directed that he be buried in paper shrouds and a tile coffin.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠定遠佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封營國公，謚忠武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Meritous Subject Who Sincerely Settles the Far and Assists the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ceremonial Parity with the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Ying with the posthumous name Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Meritous Subject Who Sincerely Settles the Far and Assists the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Master with Ceremonial Parity with the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Ying with the temple name Zhongwu, Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 子阿裏乞失鐵木兒。

translations.literal: His son was Aliqishitemuer.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Aliqishitemuer.

sentences.zh: 阿裏乞失鐵木兒，嗣父職，為興平等處行省都元帥。

translations.literal: Aliqishitemuer succeeded to his father's post as Grand Marshal of the Xingping and other districts branch secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Aliqishitemuer inherited his father's office as Grand Marshal of the branch secretariat for Xingping and the surrounding districts.

sentences.zh: 其為治一遵先政，興學養士，輕刑薄徭，雖同僚不敢私役一民。

translations.literal: In governing he wholly followed his father's policies: he promoted schools and nurtured scholars, lightened punishments and reduced levies, so that even his colleagues dared not privately conscript a single subject.
translations.idiomatic: In office he followed his father's policies to the letter—founded schools, supported scholars, eased punishments and lightened levies—so that even his colleagues would not press a single commoner into private service.

sentences.zh: 從大軍伐高麗有功。

translations.literal: He followed the main army in the campaign against Goryeo and performed meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: He served with distinction in the great campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 歲丙辰卒。

translations.literal: He died in the bingchen year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the bingchen year.

sentences.zh: 贈宣忠輔義功臣、榮祿大夫、平章政事、柱國，追封營國公，謚武襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Meritous Subject Who Proclaims Loyalty and Assists Righteousness, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Junior Grand Councillor, and Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Ying with the posthumous name Wuxiang (Martial and Assisting).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the title Meritous Subject Who Proclaims Loyalty and Assists Righteousness, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Junior Grand Councillor, and Pillar of the State; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying with the temple name Wuxiang, Martial and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 子阿臺。

translations.literal: His son was Atai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Atai.

sentences.zh: 阿臺，當襲父職，適罷行省為平灤路總管府，丁巳，憲宗命阿臺為平灤路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Atai was to inherit his father's post, but just then the branch secretariat was abolished and replaced by the Pingluan Route Pacification Commission; in the dingsi year Emperor Xianzong appointed Atai Darughachi of Pingluan Route.
translations.idiomatic: Atai was heir to his father's position, but the branch secretariat had just been abolished in favor of the Pingluan Route Pacification Commission; in the dingsi year Emperor Xianzong named Atai Darughachi of Pingluan Route.

sentences.zh: 始至，請蠲銀、鹽、酒等稅課八之一，細民不征。

translations.literal: When he first arrived he requested that one-eighth of the taxes on silver, salt, wine, and the like be remitted, and that petty households not be levied.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he petitioned for an eighth of the taxes on silver, salt, wine, and similar items to be waived, and that the poorest households be exempted entirely.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，來朝，賜金虎符。

translations.literal: When Shizu acceded to the throne, Atai came to court and was granted a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu came to the throne, Atai presented himself at court and received a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 諸侯王道出平灤，供給費銀七千五百兩，戶部不即償，阿臺自陳上前，盡取償以歸。

translations.literal: When princes and kings passed through Pingluan the cost of supplies was 7,500 taels of silver; the Ministry of Revenue did not promptly reimburse it. Atai personally reported this to the throne and recovered the full sum for return.
translations.idiomatic: When feudal lords traveled through Pingluan, provisioning them cost 7,500 taels of silver, which the Ministry of Revenue failed to repay promptly. Atai appealed directly to the emperor and secured full reimbursement.

sentences.zh: 置甲乙籍，籍民丁力，民甚便之。

translations.literal: He established A and B registers recording households' labor capacity, which greatly benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted A and B household registers that recorded each family's labor capacity, to the great convenience of the populace.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，進階懷遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to General Who Cherishes the Far.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Zhiyuan era he was promoted to General Who Cherishes the Far.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發粟賑民。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he distributed grain to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck he opened the granaries to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 或持不可，阿臺曰：「朝廷不允，願以家粟償官。」

translations.literal: Some objected that this could not be done; Atai said: "If the court does not approve, I am willing to repay the government from my household grain."
translations.idiomatic: When some objected, Atai said: "If the court refuses, I will make good the state's stores from my own household grain."

sentences.zh: 於是全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Thus a great many lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he saved a great multitude from starvation.

sentences.zh: 僚屬始至，阿臺必遺之鹽、米、羊畜、什器，曰：「非有他也，欲其不剝民耳。」

translations.literal: When subordinates first arrived, Atai always sent them salt, rice, livestock, and utensils, saying: "I have no other purpose than to keep them from exploiting the people."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a new subordinate arrived, Atai would send him salt, rice, livestock, and household goods, saying: "I do this for one reason only—that you need not squeeze the people."

sentences.zh: 姻族窮者，月有常給；

translations.literal: Impoverished kinsmen by marriage received a fixed monthly allowance;
translations.idiomatic: Poor relatives by marriage received a regular monthly stipend;

sentences.zh: 民有喪不能葬者，與之棺槨、布帛、資糧。

translations.literal: those among the people who could not afford burial were given coffins, cloth, and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: and commoners who could not afford funerals were supplied with coffins, cloth, and provisions.

sentences.zh: 灤為孤竹故國，乃廟祀伯夷、叔齊，以勵風俗。

translations.literal: Luan was the ancient state of Guzhu; he therefore established temples to Bo Yi and Shu Qi to encourage proper custom.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was the homeland of ancient Guzhu, and he erected temples to Bo Yi and Shu Qi to uphold local morals.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，進昭武大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to Illustrious Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was advanced to Illustrious Martial General.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，獻馬五百匹佐軍，世祖大喜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he presented five hundred horses to support the army; Shizu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he contributed five hundred horses to the imperial forces, to Shizu's great delight.

sentences.zh: 已而得乃顏銀甕，亟以賜之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the silver urn of Nayan was captured and promptly bestowed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Nayan's silver urn was captured soon after, the emperor at once presented it to him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年入朝，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he came to court and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he came to court and died of illness there.

sentences.zh: 賜宣力功臣、資德大夫、中書右丞、上護軍，追封永平郡公，謚忠亮。

translations.literal: He was granted Meritous Subject Who Proclaims Power, Grand Master of Assisting Virtue, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Upper Guardian of the Army; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yongping with the name Zhongliang (Loyal and Bright).
translations.idiomatic: He was honored as Meritous Subject Who Proclaims Power, Grand Master of Assisting Virtue, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Upper Guardian of the Army; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yongping with the temple name Zhongliang, Loyal and Bright.

sentences.zh: 子叠裏威失。

translations.literal: His son was Dieliweishi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Dieliweishi.

sentences.zh: 叠裏威失，少好讀書，成宗時入宿衛，授河西廉訪司僉事，拜監察御史，遷淮西廉訪副使，召為中書左司員外郎，改樞密院參議，升判官。

translations.literal: Dieliweishi loved reading from youth. Under Chengzong he entered the palace guard, was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Hexi Surveillance Commission, made Investigating Censor, transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Huaixi Surveillance Commission, summoned as Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, transferred to Consultant of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Dieliweishi was a devoted reader from boyhood. Under Chengzong he joined the palace guard, then served as Vice Commissioner of the Hexi Surveillance Commission, Investigating Censor, and Vice Commissioner of the Huaixi Surveillance Commission before being called to the Left Secretariat as Vice Director, then to the Bureau of Military Affairs as Consultant and eventually Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年，授翰林侍講學士，出為河間路總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou he was appointed Hanlin Attendant Lecturer and sent out as Pacification Commissioner of Hejian Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yanyou he was made Hanlin Attendant Lecturer and posted as Pacification Commissioner of Hejian Route.

sentences.zh: 屬歲饑，出俸金及官庫所積賑之，活數十萬人。

translations.literal: Famine struck that year; he disbursed his salary and the accumulations of the government storehouses for relief, saving several hundred thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: When famine came he spent his own salary and the reserves in the government warehouses on relief, saving hundreds of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 河間當水陸要衝，四方供億皆取給焉，迭里威失立法調遣，民便之。

translations.literal: Hejian lay at a vital junction of land and water routes; supplies from all quarters were drawn from it. Dieliweishi established regulations for dispatch, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian stood at a critical land-and-water crossroads from which supplies for the entire realm were drawn. Dieliweishi devised regulations for their distribution, greatly easing the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 復建言增置便習弓馬尉一人，益邏兵之數，於是盜賊屏息。

translations.literal: He further proposed adding one Assistant for Archery and Horsemanship and increasing patrol troops, whereupon bandits ceased their activity.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed appointing an additional Assistant for Archery and Horsemanship and increasing patrol forces, after which banditry subsided entirely.

sentences.zh: 陵州群凶為官民害，悉收系死獄中。

translations.literal: A gang of villains in Ling Prefecture were harming officials and people alike; he arrested them all and imprisoned them in the death row cells.
translations.idiomatic: A band of criminals in Ling Prefecture had been terrorizing officials and commoners alike; he rounded them up and confined them in the death row prison.

sentences.zh: 後升遼陽行省參知政事。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Vice Councillor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Vice Councillor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子鎖咬兒哈的迷失。

translations.literal: His son was Suoyaoerhadimishi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Suoyaoerhadimishi.

sentences.zh: 鎖咬兒哈的迷失，年十二，宿衛英宗潛邸，掌服御諸物。

translations.literal: Suoyaoerhadimishi, at age twelve, served in the guard of Emperor Yingzong's princely residence and managed apparel and furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve Suoyaoerhadimishi joined the guard of Yingzong's household when the latter was still heir apparent, overseeing robes and imperial accoutrements.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When Yingzong acceded to the throne, he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne he was made Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 至治元年春，詔起大剎於京西壽安山，鎖咬兒哈的迷失與御史觀音保、成珪、李謙亨上章極諫，以為東作方始，而興大役，以耗財病民，非所以祈福也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Zhizhi an edict ordered the construction of a great monastery on Shou'an Mountain west of the capital. Suoyaoerhadimishi, together with the censors Guanyinbao, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng, submitted a memorial of vehement remonstrance, holding that spring plowing had just begun, yet a great project was launched that would drain the treasury and afflict the people—this was no way to seek blessings.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first Zhizhi year an edict called for a great monastery on Shou'an Mountain west of the capital. Suoyaoerhadimishi joined Censors Guanyinbao, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng in a forceful memorial of protest: spring planting had only just begun, yet a vast public works project would drain the treasury and burden the people—hardly the way to win heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 且歲在辛酉，不宜興築。

translations.literal: Moreover, the year being xinyou, construction was inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the xinyou year was an inauspicious time for building.

sentences.zh: 初，司徒劉夔妄獻浙右民田，冒出內帑鈔六百萬貫，丞相帖木叠兒分取其半，監察御史發其奸，由是疾忌臺諫。

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister of Works Liu Kui had falsely presented civilian fields in Zheyou, fraudulently drawing six million strings of cash from the imperial treasury; Grand Councillor Temuder took half. When investigating censors exposed the fraud, he therefore came to resent the remonstrance bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Minister of Works Liu Kui had fraudulently presented civilian land in western Zhejiang, drawing six million strings of cash from the imperial treasury; Grand Councillor Temuder took half for himself. When the investigating censors exposed the scheme, he grew to hate the remonstrance offices.

sentences.zh: 至是，帖木叠兒之子瑣南為治書侍御史，密奏曰：「彼宿衛舊臣，聞事有不便，弗即入白，今訕上以揚己之直，大不敬。」

translations.literal: At this time Temuder's son Suonan was Associate Investigating Censor; he secretly memorialized: "They are old retainers of the palace guard; when they heard something amiss they did not report it at once, but now slander the sovereign to display their own integrity—this is gross disrespect."
translations.idiomatic: By then Temuder's son Suonan had become Associate Investigating Censor and secretly memorialized: "These men are former palace guards; learning of the project they did not report it promptly, but now insult the throne to parade their own righteousness—an act of gross disrespect."

sentences.zh: 帝乃殺鎖咬兒哈的迷失與觀音保，杖珪、謙亨，黥之，竄諸遐裔。

translations.literal: The emperor then executed Suoyaoerhadimishi and Guanyinbao, flogged Gui and Qianheng, branded them, and banished them to distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Suoyaoerhadimishi and Guanyinbao put to death, flogged Gui and Qianheng, branded them, and exiled them to the far reaches of the empire.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，贈鎖咬兒哈的迷失資德大夫、御史中丞、上護軍，追封永平郡公，謚貞湣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Assisting Virtue, Censor-in-Chief, and Upper Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Yongping with the name Zhenmin (Upright and Lamented).
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign Suoyaoerhadimishi was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Assisting Virtue, Censor-in-Chief, and Upper Guardian of the Army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yongping with the temple name Zhenmin, Upright and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 賜其妻子鈔五百貫、良田千畝，仍詔樹碑神道。

translations.literal: His wife and children were granted five hundred strings of cash and a thousand mu of fertile land, and an edict further ordered a stele erected on the spirit way.
translations.idiomatic: His widow and children received five hundred strings of cash and a thousand mu of fertile land, and an edict commanded a memorial stele on the spirit path.

sentences.zh: 哈剌亦哈赤北魯

translations.literal: Halayihachibeilu
translations.idiomatic: Halayihachibeilu

sentences.zh: 哈剌亦哈赤北魯，畏兀人也。

translations.literal: Halayihachibeilu was a man of the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Halayihachibeilu was an Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，習事。

translations.literal: By nature he was intelligent and quick to learn affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever by nature and readily mastered official business.

sentences.zh: 國王月仙帖木兒亦都護聞其名，自唆裏迷國徵為斷事官。

translations.literal: King Yuexiantemuer Yiduohu, hearing his reputation, summoned him from the kingdom of Suolimi as judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: King Yuexiantemuer Yiduohu, having heard of him, summoned him from Suolimi to serve as judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 月仙帖木兒卒，子八兒出阿兒忒亦都護年幼，西遼主鞠兒可汗遣使據其國，且召哈剌亦哈赤北魯，至則以為諸子師。

translations.literal: When Yuexiantemuer died, his son Baerchuaert Yiduohu was young; the ruler of Western Liao, Khan Ju'er, sent envoys to seize the state and also summoned Halayihachibeilu, who upon arrival was made tutor to the princes.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuexiantemuer's death his son Baerchuaert Yiduohu was still a boy; the ruler of Western Liao, Khan Ju'er, sent agents to occupy the kingdom and summoned Halayihachibeilu, who on arrival was appointed tutor to the royal sons.

sentences.zh: 八兒出阿兒忒聞太祖明聖，乃殺西遼使，更遣阿憐帖木兒都督等四人使西遼。

translations.literal: Baerchuaert heard that Taizu was enlightened and sagacious; he then killed the Western Liao envoy and sent Alintiemuer Dudu and three others as envoys to Western Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Taizu's wisdom and sagacity, Baerchuaert killed the Western Liao envoy and dispatched Alintiemuer Dudu and three others as envoys to Western Liao.

sentences.zh: 阿憐帖木兒都督者，哈剌亦哈赤北魯婿也。

translations.literal: Alintiemuer Dudu was Halayihachibeilu's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Alintiemuer Dudu was the son-in-law of Halayihachibeilu.

sentences.zh: 具語以其故，於是與其子月朵失野訥馳歸太祖，一見大悅，即令諸皇子受學焉。

translations.literal: He fully explained the circumstances; thereupon he and his son Yueduoshiyene galloped back to Taizu, who was greatly pleased at first sight and immediately had the imperial princes study under him.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the whole story, then rode with his son Yueduoshiyene to join Taizu, who was delighted at their first meeting and at once set them to instruct the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 仍令月朵失野訥以質子入宿衛。

translations.literal: He further ordered Yueduoshiyene to enter the palace guard as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He also required Yueduoshiyene to join the palace guard as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 從帝西征。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 至別失八里東獨山，是城空無人，帝問：「此何城也？」

translations.literal: When they reached Dushan east of Bieshibali, the city was empty of people. The emperor asked: "What city is this?"
translations.idiomatic: At Dushan east of Bieshibali they found the city deserted. The emperor asked, "What place is this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「獨山城。

translations.literal: He replied: "It is Dushan City.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Dushan City.

sentences.zh: 往歲大饑，民皆流移之它所。

translations.literal: In past years there was great famine and the people all drifted away to other places.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years famine had driven the people away to other regions.

sentences.zh: 然此地當北來要沖，宜耕種以為備。

translations.literal: Yet this place lies on the vital route from the north; it should be cultivated as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this lies on the main route from the north and ought to be farmed as a forward base.

sentences.zh: 臣昔在唆裏迷國時，有戶六十，願移居此。」

translations.literal: When I was formerly in Suolimi I had sixty households and wish to move them here."
translations.idiomatic: When I was in Suolimi I had sixty households; I would gladly resettle them here."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 遣月朵失野訥佩金符往取之，父子皆留居焉。

translations.literal: He sent Yueduoshiyene bearing a gold tally to fetch them; father and son both remained to settle there.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yueduoshiyene with a gold tally to bring them; father and son both stayed to settle the place.

sentences.zh: 後六年，太祖西征還，見田野墾辟，民物繁庶，大悅。

translations.literal: Six years later, when Taizu returned from the western campaign, he saw the fields opened for cultivation and the people and goods flourishing, and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later, when Taizu returned from the west, he found the fields under cultivation and the population thriving, and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 問哈剌亦哈赤北魯，則已死矣。

translations.literal: He inquired after Halayihachibeilu, but he had already died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked after Halayihachibeilu, only to learn that he had already died.

sentences.zh: 乃賜月朵失野訥都督印章，兼獨山城達魯花赤。

translations.literal: He then granted Yueduoshiyene the seal of a commander and concurrently made him Darughachi of Dushan City.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted Yueduoshiyene a commander's seal and appointed him Darughachi of Dushan City as well.

sentences.zh: 月朵失野訥卒，子乞赤宋忽兒，在太宗時襲爵，賜號答剌罕。

translations.literal: When Yueduoshiyene died, his son Qichisonghuer inherited the title under Taizong and was granted the designation Darqan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yueduoshiyene's death his son Qichisonghuer inherited the rank under Taizong and received the title Darqan.

sentences.zh: 子四人：曰塔塔兒，曰忽棧，曰火兒思蠻，曰月兒思蠻。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Tatuer, Huqian, Huoersiman, and Yueersiman.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Tatuer, Huqian, Huoersiman, and Yueersiman.

sentences.zh: 阿鄰帖木兒，善國書，多聞識，歷事累朝，由翰林待制累遷榮祿大夫、翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Alintiemuer was skilled in the national script and widely learned; he served through successive reigns, rising from Hanlin Attendant Drafting Official to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Hanlin Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Alintiemuer was adept in the Uyghur script and deeply learned; serving successive reigns, he rose from Hanlin Attendant Drafting Official to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Hanlin Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，以舊學日侍左右，陳說祖宗以來及古先哲王嘉言善行。

translations.literal: Under Yingzong, as an old scholar he attended daily at the sovereign's side, expounding the worthy words and deeds of the ancestors since founding and of the sage kings of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yingzong he attended daily as an elder scholar, recounting the worthy words and deeds of the founding ancestors and the sage kings of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 翻譯諸經，紀錄故實，總治諸王、駙馬、番國朝會之事。

translations.literal: He translated the scriptures, recorded historical facts, and oversaw the affairs of princes, imperial sons-in-law, and foreign tributary audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He translated canonical texts, recorded historical matters, and managed audiences for princes, imperial sons-in-law, and foreign tributaries.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，北迎明宗入正大統，一見歡甚，顧左右曰：「此朕師也。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli, when Mingzong was welcomed from the north to assume the great succession, he was overjoyed at first sight and said to those beside him: "This is my teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianli reign, when Mingzong was escorted from the north to take the throne, he was delighted at their first meeting and told those around him, "This is my teacher."

sentences.zh: 天歷三年，進光祿大夫、知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianli he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of the Classics Lectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Tianli year he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of the Classics Lectures.

sentences.zh: 子曰沙剌班，曰禿忽魯，曰六十，曰咱納祿。

translations.literal: His sons were Shalaban, Tuhulu, Liushi, and Zanalu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shalaban, Tuhulu, Liushi, and Zanalu.

sentences.zh: 沙剌班，累拜中書平章政事、大司徒、宣政院使。

translations.literal: Shalaban was repeatedly appointed Junior Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, Grand Minister of Education, and Commissioner of the Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shalaban rose through repeated appointments as Junior Grand Councillor, Grand Minister of Education, and Commissioner of the Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 塔塔統阿

translations.literal: Tatatonga
translations.idiomatic: Tatatonga

sentences.zh: 塔塔統阿，畏兀人也。

translations.literal: Tatatonga was a man of the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Tatatonga was an Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 性聰慧，善言論，深通本國文字。

translations.literal: By nature he was intelligent and skilled in discourse, with deep mastery of his native script.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever and articulate, with a thorough command of the Uyghur script.

sentences.zh: 乃蠻大敭可汗尊之為傅，掌其金印及錢谷。

translations.literal: The Great Khan of the Naiman honored him as tutor and placed the gold seal and finances in his charge.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Khan of the Naiman honored him as tutor and entrusted him with the gold seal and the treasury.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，乃蠻國亡，塔塔統阿懷印逃去，俄就擒。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned westward the Naiman state perished; Tatatonga fled clutching the seal but was soon captured.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizu's western campaign the Naiman kingdom fell; Tatatonga fled with the seal hidden on his person but was captured shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝詰之曰：「大敭人民疆土，悉歸於我矣，汝負印何之？」

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned him, saying: "The Dayang people's lands and territory have all come under me—where are you going bearing the seal?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor interrogated him: "The Naiman people and their lands have all submitted to me. Where do you think you are going with that seal?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣職也，將以死守，欲求故主授之耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "It is my office; I intend to guard it unto death, seeking only to hand it to my former lord.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "It is my duty. I mean to guard it with my life and deliver it only to my former master.

sentences.zh: 安敢有他！」

translations.literal: How dare I have any other intention!"
translations.idiomatic: I would never dream of anything else!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「忠孝人也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "A man of loyalty and filial piety!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "A man of true loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 問是印何用，對曰：「出納錢谷，委任人材，一切事皆用之，以為信驗耳。」

translations.literal: He asked what the seal was used for, and Tatatonga replied: "For disbursing and receiving funds and grain, appointing men of talent—all affairs employ it as proof of authority."
translations.idiomatic: He asked what purpose the seal served. Tatatonga replied: "It governs the treasury and granaries, authorizes appointments—every transaction relies on it as proof of legitimacy."

sentences.zh: 帝善之，命居左右。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved and ordered him to remain at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and had him stay close at hand.

sentences.zh: 是後凡有制旨，始用印章，仍命掌之。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever imperial orders were issued, the seal was first employed, and he was again ordered to keep charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: From then on imperial decrees were stamped with the seal for the first time, and Tatatonga was entrusted with its custody.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝深知本國文字乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Do you thoroughly understand your native script?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "Do you have a thorough mastery of your people's writing?"

sentences.zh: 塔塔統阿悉以所蘊對，稱旨，遂命教太子諸王以畏兀字書國言。

translations.literal: Tatatonga answered fully from all he knew, pleasing the Emperor, who then ordered him to teach the crown prince and princes to write the national language in Uyghur script.
translations.idiomatic: Tatatonga answered with everything he knew and satisfied the Emperor, who then charged him with teaching the crown prince and the princes to write Mongolian in the Uyghur script.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，命司內府玉璽金帛。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, he was ordered to manage the inner palace jade seal, gold, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession Tatatonga was appointed keeper of the inner palace jade seal, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 命其妻吾和利氏為皇子哈剌察兒乳母，時加賜予。

translations.literal: His wife Wuheli was appointed wet nurse to Prince Qarachar, and he was given additional gifts from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Wuheli was made wet nurse to Prince Qarachar, and he received frequent additional grants.

sentences.zh: 塔塔統阿召諸子諭之曰：「上以汝母鞠育太子，賜予甚厚，汝等豈宜有之，當先供太子用，有餘則可分受。

translations.literal: Tatatonga summoned his sons and instructed them: "The Emperor, because your mother nursed the crown prince, has granted us very generously—how should you keep such things for yourselves? First supply the prince's needs; whatever remains may be shared among you.
translations.idiomatic: Tatatonga gathered his sons and told them: "Because your mother nursed the crown prince, the Emperor has been lavish in his gifts. You must not keep such riches for yourselves. See to the prince's needs first; only what remains may be divided among you.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，顧侍臣曰：「塔塔統阿以朕所賜先供太子，其廉介可知矣。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he turned to his attendants and said: "Tatatonga puts what I have granted him first to the prince's use—his integrity is plain to see."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this he said to his attendants: "Tatatonga uses my gifts first for the prince—that shows how upright and scrupulous he is."

sentences.zh: 由是數加禮遇。

translations.literal: From this he repeatedly increased his honors and favor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Emperor repeatedly singled him out for honors.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of an illness.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，贈中奉大夫，追封雁門郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Distinguished Service and enfeoffed as Duke of Yanmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 3 he was posthumously created Grand Master for Distinguished Service and enfeoffed as Duke of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 子四人：長玉笏迷失，次力渾迷失，次速羅海，次篤綿。

translations.literal: He had four sons: the eldest, Yahumishi; next, Lihunmishi; next, Suluhai; and youngest, Dumian.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: the eldest Yahumishi, then Lihunmishi, then Suluhai, and the youngest Dumian.

sentences.zh: 玉笏迷失，少有勇略，渾都海叛於三盤，時玉笏迷失守護皇孫脫脫營壘，率其眾與渾都海戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Yahumishi, courageous and resourceful from youth, when Qunduqai rebelled at Sanpan was defending the camp of the imperial grandson Toto; he led his men to battle Qunduqai and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yahumishi showed courage and tactical skill even as a young man. When Qunduqai rebelled at Sanpan, Yahumishi was defending the camp of the imperial grandson Toto; he led his forces against Qunduqai and routed him.

sentences.zh: 追至只必勒，適遇阿藍答兒與之合兵，復戰，玉笏迷失死之。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Jibile, he happened to meet Alanar, who joined forces with the enemy; they fought again, and Yahumishi died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the enemy to Jibile, where Alanar reinforced Qunduqai's army. They fought again, and Yahumishi was killed.

sentences.zh: 力渾迷失，有膂力，嘗獵於野，與眾相失，遇盜三人，欲奪其衣，力渾迷失搏之，盡仆，遂縛以還。

translations.literal: Lihunmishi had great physical strength. Once while hunting in the wild he became separated from his party, met three bandits who sought to strip him of his clothes, wrestled with them, knocked them all down, bound them, and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: Lihunmishi was immensely strong. Once while hunting he became separated from his companions and was set upon by three robbers who tried to take his clothing. He fought them, knocked all three to the ground, bound them, and marched them back in captivity.

sentences.zh: 帝召見，選力士與之角，無與敵者。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him and selected strongmen to wrestle with him; none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him before the court and pitted him against the palace's strongest wrestlers; none could defeat him.

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，賜金，令行宿衛。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired him, granted him gold, and ordered him to serve in the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed, the Emperor rewarded him with gold and appointed him to the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 速羅海，襲父職，仍命司內府玉璽金帛。

translations.literal: Suluhai inherited his father's office and was again ordered to manage the inner palace jade seal, gold, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Suluhai succeeded to his father's post and was again entrusted with the inner palace jade seal, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 嶽璘帖穆爾

translations.literal: Yuelintiemuer
translations.idiomatic: Yuelintiemuer

sentences.zh: 嶽璘帖穆爾，回鶻人，畏兀國相暾欲谷之裔也。

translations.literal: Yuelintiemuer was a Uyghur, a descendant of Tun Yugu, Chancellor of the Uyghur state.
translations.idiomatic: Yuelintiemuer was a Uyghur, descended from Tun Yugu, chancellor of the Uyghur kingdom.

sentences.zh: 其兄仳理伽普華，年十六，襲國相、答剌罕。

translations.literal: His elder brother Bilijiahua, at age sixteen, inherited the offices of state chancellor and darughachi.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Bilijiahua succeeded at sixteen to the offices of state chancellor and darughachi.

sentences.zh: 時西契丹方強，威制畏兀，命太師僧少監來臨其國，驕恣用權，奢淫自奉。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Liao were powerful and dominated the Uyghurs; they sent the Grand Preceptor Monk Shaojian to oversee the country. He was arrogant and arbitrary in his authority, indulging in luxury for himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Western Liao held the Uyghurs in tight subjection and sent the Grand Preceptor Shaojian to govern the country. He ruled with arrogant caprice and lived in lavish self-indulgence.

sentences.zh: 畏兀王患之，謀於仳理伽普華曰：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: The Uyghur king was troubled by this and consulted Bilijiahua: "What plan can we devise?"
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur king was deeply troubled and asked Bilijiahua: "What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「能殺少監，挈吾眾歸大蒙古國，彼且震駭矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If we can kill Shaojian and lead our people to submit to the Great Mongol State, they will be shaken with terror."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Kill Shaojian, bring our people over to the Great Mongol State, and the Liao will be thrown into panic."

sentences.zh: 遂率眾圍少監，斬之。

translations.literal: He then led his followers to surround Shaojian and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his men to surround Shaojian and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 以功加號仳理傑忽底，進授明別吉，妻號赫思叠林。

translations.literal: For this merit Bilijiahua was given the additional title Bili Jiehudi, promoted to Mingbieji, and his wife was styled Hesidielin.
translations.idiomatic: For this service Bilijiahua received the added title Bili Jiehudi, was promoted to Mingbieji, and his wife was granted the title Hesidielin.

sentences.zh: 左右有疾其功者，譖於其王曰：「少監珥珠，先王寶也，仳理伽普華匿之，盍急索勿失。」

translations.literal: Some at court, envious of his achievement, slandered him to the king: "The pearl earrings Shaojian wore were treasures of the former king; Bilijiahua has hidden them—hurry and demand them before they are lost."
translations.idiomatic: Envious courtiers slandered him to the king: "The pearl earrings Shaojian wore were heirlooms of the former king. Bilijiahua has concealed them—seize them at once before they vanish."

sentences.zh: 其王怒，索寶甚急。

translations.literal: The king grew angry and demanded the treasure with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The king flew into a rage and pressed the demand fiercely.

sentences.zh: 仳理伽普華度無以自明，乃亡附太祖，賜以金虎符、獅紐銀印、金螭椅一、衣金直孫校尉四人，仍食二十三郡。

translations.literal: Bilijiahua, seeing no way to clear himself, fled and submitted to Taizu, who granted him a gold tiger tally, a silver seal with lion cord, one gold dragon chair, four guards in gold-trimmed uniforms, and revenues from twenty-three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to prove his innocence, Bilijiahua fled to Taizu and submitted. Taizu rewarded him with a gold tiger tally, a silver seal with lion tassel, a gold dragon chair, four guards in gold-trimmed livery, and the revenues of twenty-three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 繼又賜銀五萬兩。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally granted fifty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given fifty thousand taels of silver as well.

sentences.zh: 以弟岳璘帖穆爾為質。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuelintiemuer was sent as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuelintiemuer was left at court as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 仳理伽普華以疾卒。

translations.literal: Bilijiahua died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bilijiahua died of an illness.

sentences.zh: 李楨，字幹臣。

translations.literal: Li Zhen, styled Ganchen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen, courtesy name Ganchen.

sentences.zh: 其先，西夏國族子也。

translations.literal: His ancestors were scions of the Xi Xia royal clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family were descendants of the Western Xia imperial house.

sentences.zh: 金末，楨以經童中選。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin dynasty, Zhen was selected in the classics youth examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the waning years of the Jin dynasty he was chosen in the classics prodigy examination.

sentences.zh: 既長，入為質子，以文學得近侍，太宗嘉之，賜名玉出幹必阇赤。

translations.literal: When he came of age he entered service as a hostage; through his literary attainments he gained access to the inner court. Taizong was pleased and bestowed on him the name Yuchu Ganbishchi.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew to adulthood he was sent as a hostage to the Mongols. His literary talent won him a place close to the throne. Taizong was impressed and granted him the Mongol name Yuchu Ganbishchi.

sentences.zh: 從皇子闊出伐金，帝命之曰：「凡軍中事，須訪楨以行。」

translations.literal: Following Prince Kuochu in the campaign against Jin, the Emperor ordered: "In all military affairs you must consult Zhen before acting."
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Prince Kuochu in the war against the Jin, the Emperor instructed: "On every military matter consult Zhen before you act."

sentences.zh: 及下河南諸郡，闊出遣楨偕吉登哥往唐、鄧二州數民實，兵余歲凶，流散十八九。

translations.literal: After the reduction of the Henan commanderies, Kuochu sent Zhen together with Jidengge to Tang and Deng prefectures to count the population; after the wars and years of famine, eight or nine tenths had scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern Henan districts fell, Kuochu dispatched Zhen with Jidengge to Tang and Deng to assess the population. Between the ravages of war and successive bad harvests, nearly nine tenths of the people had fled.

sentences.zh: 楨至，賑恤饑寒，歸者如市。

translations.literal: When Zhen arrived he relieved hunger and cold; returnees came as thick as a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen arrived he organized relief for the hungry and the cold, and refugees returned in droves.

sentences.zh: 十年，從大將察罕下淮甸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed the general Chaghan in the reduction of the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he followed General Chaghan in the conquest of the Huai basin.

sentences.zh: 楨以功佩金符，授軍前行中書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: Zhen, for his merit, was granted a gold tally and appointed Left and Right Department Director of the Field Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Zhen received a gold tally and was appointed director of the left and right departments of the Field Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 楨奏尋訪天下儒士，令所在優贍之。

translations.literal: Zhen memorialized requesting a search for scholars throughout the realm and ordering local authorities to support them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen submitted a memorial asking that scholars be sought out across the empire and given generous support wherever they were found.

sentences.zh: 十三年，師圍壽春，天雨不止，楨言於察罕曰：「頓師城下，暑雨疫作，將有不利。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the army besieged Shouchun and rain fell without cease, Zhen said to Chaghan: "To halt the army beneath the walls while summer rains breed pestilence will bring misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen, as the army lay siege to Shouchun under unending rain, Zhen told Chaghan: "Keeping troops idle beneath the walls while summer rains breed plague will end badly.

sentences.zh: 且城久拒命，破必屠之，則生靈何辜。

translations.literal: Moreover, the city has long defied our commands; if we take it we shall surely massacre—what crime have the common people committed?
translations.idiomatic: And the city has resisted for so long that if we storm it we will slaughter indiscriminately—what have the civilians done to deserve that?

sentences.zh: 請退舍數里，身往招之。」

translations.literal: I ask that we withdraw several li and that I go in person to summon their surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Pull the army back a few li and let me go alone to negotiate their surrender."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Chaghan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan assented.

sentences.zh: 楨遂單騎入敵壘，曉以利害，明日，與其將二人率眾來降。

translations.literal: Zhen then rode alone into the enemy camp, explained advantage and harm, and the next day two of their generals led the people in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen rode unescorted into the enemy camp, laid out the costs and benefits of resistance, and the next day two of their commanders came over with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 以功賜銀五千兩。

translations.literal: For this merit he was granted five thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was rewarded with five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 楨表言：「襄陽乃吳、蜀之要沖，宋之喉襟，得之則可為他日取宋之基本。」

translations.literal: Zhen submitted a memorial: "Xiangyang is the strategic junction of Wu and Shu, the throat of Song—if we secure it, it can serve as the foundation for a future conquest of Song."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wrote to the throne: "Xiangyang guards the route between Wu and Shu—it is the throat of Song territory. Holding it would give us the base we need for a future campaign against the Song."

sentences.zh: 定宗嘉其言。

translations.literal: Dingzong commended his words.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong praised the proposal.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，賜虎符，授襄陽軍馬萬戶。

translations.literal: In the gengxu year he was granted a tiger tally and appointed Military Ten-thousand Household of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In gengxu he received a tiger tally and was made commander of the Xiangyang military household.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，憲宗命楨率師巡哨襄樊。

translations.literal: In the bingchen year Mizong ordered Zhen to lead troops in patrol and reconnaissance at Xiang-Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In bingchen Mizong ordered Zhen to lead troops on patrol around Xiangyang and Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝親征，召楨同議事。

translations.literal: In the wuwu year the Emperor personally took the field and summoned Zhen to consult on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In wuwu the Emperor led the campaign in person and summoned Zhen to council.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，卒於合州，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn he died at Hezhou, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Hezhou in the ninth month of autumn, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 速哥，蒙古怯烈氏，世傳李唐外族。

translations.literal: Suge was of the Mongol Qilie clan, which for generations claimed descent from a Tang imperial kinship line.
translations.idiomatic: Suge was a Mongol of the Qilie clan, a family that traced its descent to a Tang imperial consort's kin.

sentences.zh: 父懷都，事太祖，嘗從飲班術尼河水。

translations.literal: His father Huaidu served Taizu and once drank from the waters of the Onon River with him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaidu had served Taizu and once shared a drink from the Onon River at his side.

sentences.zh: 速哥為人外若質直，而內實沈勇有謀，雅為太宗所知。

translations.literal: Suge outwardly appeared plain and straightforward, but inwardly was deep, brave, and resourceful; he was well known to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Suge seemed plainspoken and blunt on the surface, but he was inwardly shrewd, courageous, and clever—and Taizong knew his worth.

sentences.zh: 命使金，因俾覘其虛實，語之曰：「即不還，子孫無憂不富貴也。」

translations.literal: He was ordered to envoy to Jin and, in the same breath, to reconnoiter their strength and weakness. The Emperor told him: "Even if you do not return, your descendants need not worry—they will not lack wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent him as envoy to the Jin and charged him to scout their strengths and weaknesses. "Even if you never come back," he said, "your descendants will want for nothing."

sentences.zh: 速哥頓首曰：「臣死，職耳。

translations.literal: Suge bowed and said: "To die is my duty.
translations.idiomatic: Suge kowtowed and replied: "Death is simply my duty.

sentences.zh: 奉陛下威命以行，可無慮也。」

translations.literal: Carrying out Your Majesty's august command on this mission—there is nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: I go bearing Your Majesty's authority—there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜所常御馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and granted him the horse he himself regularly rode.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and gave him his own riding horse.

sentences.zh: 至河，金人閉之舟中，七日始登南岸，又三旬乃達汴。

translations.literal: Reaching the Yellow River, the Jin kept him confined aboard a boat; only after seven days did he reach the south bank, and after another thirty days he arrived at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yellow River the Jin locked him aboard a boat; seven days passed before he was allowed ashore on the south bank, and another month before he reached Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 及見金主，曰：「天子念爾土地日狹，民力日疲，故遣我致命，爾能共修歲幣，通好不絕，則轉禍為福矣。」

translations.literal: When he met the Jin emperor he said: "Our lord, mindful that your lands grow daily narrower and your people daily more exhausted, has sent me to deliver his message: if you can jointly restore the annual tribute and keep friendly relations unbroken, disaster may be turned to blessing."
translations.idiomatic: When he faced the Jin emperor he said: "Our khan sees your territory shrinking and your people worn down, and has sent me with this message: restore the tribute payments and keep the peace, and you may yet turn calamity into fortune."

sentences.zh: 謁者令下拜，速哥曰：「我大國使，為爾屈乎！」

translations.literal: The usher ordered him to bow; Suge said: "I am an envoy of a great state—shall I bow before you?"
translations.idiomatic: An attendant ordered him to prostrate himself. Suge said: "I am envoy of a great power—do you expect me to kowtow to you?"

sentences.zh: 金主壯之，取金卮飲之酒曰：「歸語汝主，必欲加兵，敢率精銳以相周旋，歲幣非所聞也。」

translations.literal: The Jin emperor admired him, took a gold goblet and drank to him, saying: "Return and tell your lord: if he must send armies, I dare lead elite troops to match him—annual tribute is not a word I recognize."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor was impressed. He raised a gold cup and drank to Suge: "Tell your khan that if he wants war, I will meet his best troops in battle. As for tribute—that word means nothing to me."

sentences.zh: 速哥飲畢，即懷金卮以出。

translations.literal: When Suge had finished drinking, he put the gold goblet in his robe and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Suge finished his drink, tucked the gold cup into his robe, and walked out.

sentences.zh: 速哥雖佯為不智，而默識其地理厄塞、城郭人民之強弱。

translations.literal: Though Suge feigned simple-mindedness, he silently took note of the terrain's passes and barriers and the relative strength of cities and populations.
translations.idiomatic: Suge played the fool, but all the while he memorized the mountain passes, the fortifications, and the strength of every city and garrison.

sentences.zh: 既復命，備以虛實告，且以所懷金卮獻。

translations.literal: On his return he reported fully on their condition and presented the gold goblet he had taken.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he gave a full intelligence report and presented the gold cup he had carried off.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「我得金於汝手中矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with delight: "I have obtained Jin from your hand."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed: "You have put Jin in the palm of my hand."

sentences.zh: 復以賜之。

translations.literal: He returned it to him as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Then he gave the cup back to Suge.

sentences.zh: 始下令征兵南伐。

translations.literal: The order to levy troops for the southern campaign was then issued.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the Emperor order the levies for the southern invasion.

sentences.zh: 兵至河北岸，方舟欲渡，金軍陳於河南，帝令儀衛導速哥居中行，親率偏師乘陣西策馬沙河。

translations.literal: When the army reached the north bank of the Yellow River and prepared boats to cross, Jin forces formed ranks on the south bank. The Emperor ordered the ceremonial guard to lead Suge in the center column while he personally led a detached force westward to gallop along the Sha River.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the north bank and readied boats to cross, Jin troops lined the south bank. The Emperor put Suge at the head of the center column under full ceremonial escort, while he himself led a flanking force west along the Sha River.

sentences.zh: 會睿宗軍亦由襄、鄧至，兩軍夾攻之。

translations.literal: When Prince Regent's army also arrived via Xiang and Deng, the two forces attacked from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Regent's army came up through Xiang and Deng, and the two Mongol forces caught the Jin in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 及金亡，詔賜金護駕士五人，曰：「此以旌汝為使之不辱也。」

translations.literal: After the fall of Jin, an edict granted him five gold bodyguards, saying: "This is to honor the fact that as envoy you did not disgrace your mission."
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin fell, the Emperor granted him five golden bodyguards, saying: "This marks how proudly you bore our standard as envoy."

sentences.zh: 昔使過崞州，崞人盜殺其良馬，至是，兼以崞民賜之。

translations.literal: Long ago on his embassy he had passed through Guo prefecture, where the people had stolen and killed his fine horse; now he was additionally granted the populace of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Years earlier, passing through Guo on his embassy, locals had stolen and killed his best horse. Now he was given the people of Guo as compensation.

sentences.zh: 歲乙未，帝從容謂速哥曰：「我將官汝，西域、中原，惟汝擇之。」

translations.literal: In the yiwei year the Emperor said casually to Suge: "I intend to appoint you to office—of the Western Regions and the Central Plains, choose as you will."
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year the Emperor said to Suge at ease: "I am about to give you a post—choose for yourself between the Western Regions and China proper."

sentences.zh: 速哥再拜曰：「幸甚！

translations.literal: Suge bowed twice and said: "Great fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Suge bowed twice and said: "I am deeply honored!

sentences.zh: 臣意中原為便。」

translations.literal: In my mind the Central Plains would be more suitable."
translations.idiomatic: I would prefer the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「西山之境，八達以北，汝其主之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The lands west of the mountains, north of Bada—there you shall rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The territory west of the mountains, north of Bada—that is yours to govern.

sentences.zh: 汝於城中構大樓，居其上，使人皆仰望汝，汝俯而諭之，顧不偉乎！」

translations.literal: Build a great tower in the city and dwell atop it, so that all may look up to you as you look down to instruct them—is that not magnificent!"
translations.idiomatic: Build a great tower in your city and live at the top, so everyone looks up to you while you look down and give your orders—is that not splendid?"

sentences.zh: 乃以為山西大達魯花赤。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Grand Darughachi of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Darughachi of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 受命方出，有回回六人訟事不實，將抵罪，遇諸途，急止監者曰：「姑緩其刑，當入奏。」

translations.literal: Just as he had received his appointment and was leaving, six Muslims whose lawsuit had been found false and who were about to be punished met him on the road; he urgently stopped the escort and said: "For now stay the punishment—I must enter a memorial."
translations.idiomatic: He had barely left the palace with his commission when he encountered six Muslim merchants convicted of a fraudulent lawsuit and about to be punished. He stopped their guards on the spot: "Hold the execution—I must speak to the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 復見帝曰：「此六人者，名著西域，徒以小罪盡誅之，恐非所以懷遠人也。

translations.literal: He saw the Emperor again and said: "These six men are famous throughout the Western Regions; to execute them all for minor offenses would surely not be the way to win over distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Emperor and said: "These six are well known across the Western Regions. To slaughter them over a petty offense is no way to win distant peoples to our rule.

sentences.zh: 願以賜臣，臣得困辱之，使自悔悟遷善，為他日用，殺之無益也。」

translations.literal: I ask that they be granted to me; I can humiliate and chastise them so that they may repent and turn to goodness, to be of use another day—to kill them would benefit nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Give them to me instead. I will humble and discipline them until they repent and reform—they may yet prove useful. Executing them serves no purpose."

sentences.zh: 帝意解，召六人謂之曰：「生汝者速哥也，其竭力事之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger eased; he summoned the six and told them: "Suge has saved your lives—serve him with all your strength."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor relented and called the six before him: "Suge gave you your lives. Serve him faithfully."

sentences.zh: 至雲中，皆釋之。

translations.literal: Reaching Yunzhong, he released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Once they reached Yunzhong he set them all free.

sentences.zh: 後有至大官者。

translations.literal: Later some rose to high office.
translations.idiomatic: Some of them later rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 其寬大愛人多類此。

translations.literal: His magnanimity and care for others were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His generosity and humane concern for others were characteristic in this way.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠翊運同德功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封宣寧王，謚忠襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the honorific Meritous Loyal Supporter of the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian with the same ceremonials as the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Prince Xuanning and given the posthumous name Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Meritous Loyal Supporter of the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State; enfeoffed posthumously as Prince Xuanning with the temple name Loyal Helper.

sentences.zh: 子六人：曰長罕，曰玉呂忽都，曰撒合裏都，曰忽蘭，曰忽都兒不花，曰不花。

translations.literal: He had six sons: named Chaghan, Yuluhudu, Sagelidu, Hulan, Quduerbuhua, and Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Chaghan, Yuluhudu, Sagelidu, Hulan, Quduerbuhua, and Buhua.

sentences.zh: 長罕、玉呂忽都、撒合裏都，皆從兀魯赤太子出征，以戰功顯。

translations.literal: Chaghan, Yuluhudu, and Sagelidu all followed Prince Uruchi on campaign and distinguished themselves through military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan, Yuluhudu, and Sagelidu all campaigned under Prince Uruchi and won fame in battle.

sentences.zh: 忽蘭之母以後戚故，得襲職。

translations.literal: Hulan's mother, being related to the empress by marriage, was permitted to inherit the office.
translations.idiomatic: Hulan inherited the post through his mother, who was related to the imperial consort's family.

sentences.zh: 鉏強植弱，均役平刑，闔郡賴以安輯。

translations.literal: He uprooted the strong and planted the weak, equalized corvée and tempered punishments, and the whole commandery relied on him for peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: He checked the powerful, protected the weak, equalized labor service and made punishments more equitable—and the whole commandery lived in peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 乙未之抄戶籍也，前賜崞人已入官籍，更賜山西戶三百。

translations.literal: At the household registration survey of yiwei, the people of Guo previously granted him had already entered the official registers; he was additionally granted three hundred households in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the yiwei household census the Guo families earlier granted him had already been entered on the official rolls, so he was given three hundred Shanxi households in addition.

sentences.zh: 西方多盜，郡縣捕不得，則法當計所失物直倍償，郡縣苦之。

translations.literal: In the western regions there were many bandits; when the counties and districts could not capture them, by law they had to calculate the value of lost goods and pay double compensation—the counties and districts found this grievous.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rampant in the west, and whenever counties failed to make arrests the law required them to compensate victims at double the value of stolen goods—a burden the local administrations bitterly resented.

sentences.zh: 有甄軍判者，率群盜往來阜平、曲陽間，殺人渾源界而奪之財。

translations.literal: There was one Zhen Junpan, who led a band of robbers traveling between Fuping and Quyang, killing people in the Hunyuan borderlands and seizing their wealth.
translations.idiomatic: One bandit chief, Zhen Junpan, led a gang that ranged between Fuping and Quyang, murdering travelers on the Hunyuan frontier and plundering their goods.

sentences.zh: 縣以失捕當償，忽蘭曰：「此大盜也，縣豈能制哉！」

translations.literal: The county, being liable to pay for failure to capture them, Hulan said: "This is a great outlaw—how could the county restrain him!"
translations.idiomatic: Faced with liability for the failed arrest, Hulan said, "This man is a major brigand—the county is in no position to bring him to heel!"

sentences.zh: 即遣千人捕甄殺之，剿捕其餘黨，其害乃除。

translations.literal: Immediately he dispatched a thousand men to capture and kill Zhen, mopped up the rest of the band, and the menace was removed.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent a thousand men after Zhen, killed him, hunted down the remaining accomplices, and at last rid the region of the scourge.

sentences.zh: 忽蘭性純篤，然酷好佛，嘗施千金修龍宮寺，建金輪大會，供僧萬人。

translations.literal: Hulan's nature was simple and sincere, yet he intensely loved Buddhism; once he donated a thousand in gold to repair Longgong Temple, established a Golden Wheel Assembly, and supplied ten thousand monks.
translations.idiomatic: Hulan was upright and sincere by nature, but devoted to Buddhism: he once gave a thousand ounces of gold to restore Longgong Temple, convened a great Golden Wheel Dharma assembly, and fed ten thousand monks.

sentences.zh: 卒年四十二。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太保、金紫光祿大夫、上柱國，追封雲國公，謚康忠。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred Grand Preceptor, Grand Imperial Bright-Gold Light Grand Master, and Supreme Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yun, with the posthumous title Kangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was honored as Grand Preceptor, given the titles of Gold-and-Purple Light Grand Master and Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Yun, and granted the temple name Kangzhong—"Peaceful and Loyal."

sentences.zh: 子天德於思，穎悟過人，世祖聞其賢，令襲父爵，養母完顏氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: His son Tiandesiyu was sharp-witted beyond ordinary men; Shizu heard of his worth and ordered him to inherit his father's rank; he supported his mother Lady Wanyan and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tiandesiyu was unusually quick and clever. When Shizu learned of his merit he ordered him to succeed to his father's title; he cared for his mother, Lady Wanyan, and won renown for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 自中山北來，適有邊釁，天德於思督造兵甲，撫循其民，無有寧息，形容盡瘁。

translations.literal: Coming north from Zhongshan, there happened to be trouble on the frontier; Tiandesiyu supervised the manufacture of armor and weapons, soothed and guided the people, and had no moment of rest—his appearance was utterly worn.
translations.idiomatic: On his journey north from Zhongshan a border crisis erupted. Tiandesiyu oversaw the forging of arms and armor and looked after the people without a moment's respite, until he was worn to the bone.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之，賜馴豹、名鷹，使得縱獵禁地，當時眷顧最號優渥。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of this and commended him, bestowing a trained leopard and a fine hawk, and allowing him to hunt in forbidden preserves—the favor he enjoyed at the time was called the most generous of all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his service and rewarded him with a trained leopard and a prized hawk, with license to hunt in the imperial preserves—no courtier of the day enjoyed richer favor.

sentences.zh: 卒年三十九。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅、儀同三司、上柱國，追封雲國公，謚顯毅。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred Grand Tutor, Three Excellencies of Equal Rank, and Supreme Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yun, with the posthumous title Xianyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor with the rank equal to the Three Excellencies and as Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Yun, and given the temple name Xianyi—"Illustrious and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 子孫世多顯貴云。

translations.literal: His descendants for generations were many in eminence and honor, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants, it is said, remained prominent for generations.

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒

translations.literal: Manggesaer
translations.idiomatic: Manggesaer

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒，察哈劄剌兒氏。

translations.literal: Manggesaer, of the Chaghar Jala'ir clan.
translations.idiomatic: Manggesaer belonged to the Chaghar Jala'ir clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖赤老溫愷赤，祖搠阿，父那海，並事烈祖。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Chilaun Qiqi, his grandfather Shuo'a, and his father Nhai—all served the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chilaun Qiqi, his grandfather Shuo'a, and his father Nhai had all served the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 及太祖嗣位，年尚幼，所部多叛亡，搠阿獨不去。

translations.literal: When Taizu succeeded to the throne, he was still young; many of his followers rebelled and fled, but Shuo'a alone did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu came to power he was still young; most of his followers deserted, but Shuo'a alone stayed loyal.

sentences.zh: 皇弟槊只哈撒兒陰擿之去，亦謝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor's younger brother Jochi Qasar secretly urged him to leave, but he declined and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's brother Jochi Qasar tried secretly to persuade him to abandon the young lord, but Shuo'a refused to go.

sentences.zh: 搠阿精騎射，帝甚愛之，號為默爾傑，華言善射之尤者也。

translations.literal: Shuo'a was skilled in mounted archery; the Emperor deeply loved him and styled him Mo'erjie—in Chinese, the foremost of those who shoot well.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo'a was a master of mounted archery, and the emperor cherished him, giving him the Mongol title Mo'erjie—"Supreme Archer," the finest marksman of the age.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與賊遇，將戰，有二飛鶩至，帝命搠阿謝之。

translations.literal: Once the Emperor encountered bandits and was about to fight; two wild ducks in flight arrived, and the Emperor ordered Shuo'a to shoot them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as the emperor was about to engage bandits, two ducks flew overhead and he ordered Shuo'a to bring them down.

sentences.zh: 請曰：「射其雄乎？

translations.literal: Shuo'a asked: "Shall I shoot the drake?
translations.idiomatic: Shuo'a asked, "Shall I take the drake?

sentences.zh: 抑雌者乎？」

translations.literal: Or the hen?"
translations.idiomatic: Or the hen?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「雄者。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The drake."
translations.idiomatic: "The drake," the emperor said."

sentences.zh: 搠阿一發墜其雄。

translations.literal: With one shot Shuo'a brought down the drake.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo'a loosed a single arrow and dropped the drake.

sentences.zh: 賊望見，驚曰：「是善射若此，飛鳥且不能逃，況人乎！」

translations.literal: The bandits saw this and cried in alarm: "If his archery is this good, not even birds can escape—how much less men!"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits saw it and cried out in alarm: "A man who shoots like that—if birds cannot escape him, what chance have we!"

sentences.zh: 不戰而去。

translations.literal: Without fighting they departed.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew without a fight.

sentences.zh: 從征乃蠻，敵率銳兵鼓而進，搠阿按兵屹不動，敵止。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against the Naiman, the enemy led crack troops beating drums in advance; Shuo'a held his troops immovable as a mountain, and the enemy halted.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against the Naiman, the enemy advanced with elite troops drumming for battle; Shuo'a held his line rock-steady until the enemy halted.

sentences.zh: 俄復鼓而進，搠阿亦不動，敵卒疑畏不敢前。

translations.literal: Soon they again beat drums and advanced; Shuo'a still did not move, and the enemy at last grew suspicious and fearful and dared not press forward.
translations.idiomatic: When they drummed and charged a second time Shuo'a still did not stir; at last the enemy, unnerved, held back.

sentences.zh: 太祖征蔑裏吉，兵潰，搠阿與其弟左右力戰以衛帝。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against the Merkit and the army collapsed, Shuo'a and his younger brother fought fiercely on either side to protect the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizu's campaign against the Merkits, when the army broke, Shuo'a and his brother fought on either flank to shield the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會兀良罕哲裏馬來援，敵乃引退。

translations.literal: Just then Ulanhan Zheli came with reinforcements on horseback, and the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ulanhan Zheli arrived with reinforcements in the nick of time, and the enemy pulled back.

sentences.zh: 那海事太祖，備歷艱險，未嘗形於言，帝嘉其忠，且念其世勛，詔封懷、洛陽百七十五戶。

translations.literal: Nhai served Taizu, enduring every hardship, yet never betrayed it in speech; the Emperor praised his loyalty and, mindful of his family's hereditary merit, ordered enfeoffment with one hundred seventy-five households in Huai and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Nhai served Taizu through every peril without once complaining; the emperor commended his loyalty and, recalling generations of service, granted him one hundred seventy-five households in Huai and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒事睿宗，恭謹過其父。

translations.literal: Manggesaer served Ruizong with a respect and diligence surpassing his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Ruizong's service Manggesaer showed a deference and diligence that exceeded even his father's.

sentences.zh: 嘗從攻鳳翔，首立奇功。

translations.literal: Once, following the assault on Fengxiang, he was first to win extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Fengxiang he distinguished himself with the campaign's first great feat of arms.

sentences.zh: 定宗升為斷事官，剛明能舉職。

translations.literal: Under Dingzong he was promoted to Chief of Legal Affairs; upright and clear-sighted, he was able to fulfill his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong raised him to chief judicial officer; stern, fair, and capable, he discharged his office well.

sentences.zh: 憲宗在藩邸，深知其人。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was in his princely establishment, he knew the man well.
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince, Xianzong knew Manggesaer well and trusted his character.

sentences.zh: 從征斡羅思、阿速、欽察諸部，常身先諸將，及以所俘寶玉頒諸將，則退然一無所取。

translations.literal: Following campaigns against Rus, the Alans, the Cumans, and other peoples, he was constantly ahead of the generals; when captured jewels were distributed among the generals, he modestly took nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaigns against Rus, the Alans, the Cumans, and the other tribes he always led from the front; when looted gems were divided among the commanders he alone declined his share.

sentences.zh: 憲宗由是益重之，使治藩邸之分民。

translations.literal: Xianzong therefore valued him still more and put him in charge of the princely household's assigned people.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong thought all the more highly of him and entrusted him with the subjects assigned to the princely household.

sentences.zh: 間出遊獵，則長其軍士，動如紀律。

translations.literal: When he occasionally went out hunting, he commanded the soldiers; their movements were as disciplined as under regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Even on hunting outings he led the troops in strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 雖太后及諸嬪御小有過失，知無不言，以故邸中人咸敬憚之。

translations.literal: Even when the empress dowager and the consorts had minor faults, knowing of them he held nothing back; for this reason everyone in the princely household both respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He spared no one in the princely household—not even the empress dowager or the consorts when they erred in small matters—and for that everyone within its walls both respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 乃以為斷事官之長，其位在三公之上，猶漢之大將軍也。

translations.literal: He was therefore made head of the chiefs of legal affairs; his rank was above the Three Excellencies, like the Han Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief of all judicial officers, with rank above the Three Excellencies—the Mongol equivalent of a Han Grand General.

sentences.zh: 既拜命，出帳殿外，欹橐坐熊席，其僚列坐左右者四十人。

translations.literal: Once he had received the appointment, he went outside the tent palace, leaned against his quiver and sat on a bear-skin mat; his subordinates, forty in number, sat in rows to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the appointment he stepped outside the tent palace, set his quiver aside, and seated himself on a bearskin; forty of his lieutenants arranged themselves on either side.

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒問曰：「主上以我長此官，諸公其為我言，當以何道守官？」

translations.literal: Manggesaer asked: "The sovereign has made me head of this office—gentlemen, speak for me: by what principle should one hold office?"
translations.idiomatic: Manggesaer asked, "Our lord has put me at the head of this office. Tell me, gentlemen—by what rule should a man keep such a post?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆默然。

translations.literal: All were silent.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 又問之，有夏人和斡居下坐，進曰：「夫劄魯忽赤之道，猶宰之刲羊也，解肩者不使傷其脊，在持平而已。」

translations.literal: He asked again; a Xia man named Hefo, seated below, stepped forward and said: "The way of the jarquchi is like a butcher's slaughter of a sheep—when cutting the shoulder he must not injure the spine; it lies in holding the balance even, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed the question again, a Chinese adviser named Hefo, who sat among the junior ranks, spoke up: "The jarquchi's art is like a butcher dressing a sheep: when you cut the shoulder you must not slice the spine—the whole trick is even-handedness."

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒聞之，即起入帳內。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Manggesaer immediately rose and entered the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Manggesaer rose at once and went inside the tent.

sentences.zh: 眾不知所為，皆咎和斡失言。

translations.literal: The assembly did not know what to make of it and all blamed Hefo for his imprudent words.
translations.idiomatic: The others, baffled, blamed Hefo for having spoken out of turn.

sentences.zh: 既入，乃為帝言和斡之言善。

translations.literal: Once inside, he reported to the Emperor that Hefo's words were excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, he told the emperor that Hefo's answer was admirable.

sentences.zh: 帝召和斡，命之步，曰：「是可用之才也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Hefo and ordered him to walk forth, saying: "This is talent that can be employed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Hefo in, had him walk before him, and said, "Here is a man worth employing."

sentences.zh: 和斡由是知名。

translations.literal: From this Hefo became known.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Hefo made his name.
