sentences.zh: 定宗崩，宗王八都罕大會宗親，議立憲宗。

translations.literal: When Dingzong died, the prince Batu Khan convened a great assembly of kinsmen to deliberate installing Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: After Dingzong's death Prince Batu Khan summoned the royal clans to council to choose Xianzong as successor.

sentences.zh: 畏兀八剌曰：「失烈門，皇孫也，宜立。

translations.literal: Üitübär said: "Shiremün is the Emperor's grandson—he should be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Üitübär argued, "Shiremün is the late emperor's grandson—he is the rightful choice.

sentences.zh: 且先帝嘗言其可以君天下。」

translations.literal: Moreover the late Emperor once said that he could rule the realm."
translations.idiomatic: And Ögedei himself once declared that the boy could govern the empire."

sentences.zh: 諸大臣皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: None of the great ministers dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The senior ministers all held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒獨曰：「汝言誠是，然先皇后立定宗時，汝何不言耶？

translations.literal: Manggesaer alone said: "Your words are indeed true—yet when the late empress installed Dingzong, why did you not speak then?
translations.idiomatic: Manggesaer alone replied, "You speak truth—but where was this argument when the late empress enthroned Dingzong?

sentences.zh: 八都罕固亦遵先帝遺言也。

translations.literal: Batu Khan likewise is simply following the late Emperor's testament.
translations.idiomatic: Batu Khan, for his part, is likewise obeying the late emperor's dying words.

sentences.zh: 有異議者，吾請斬之。」

translations.literal: Whoever has a different opinion—I ask to behead him."
translations.idiomatic: Let any man who objects step forward, and I shall ask that his head be taken."

sentences.zh: 眾乃不敢異，八都罕乃奉憲宗立之。

translations.literal: The assembly then dared not dissent, and Batu Khan thereupon installed Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared oppose him, and Batu enthroned Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 憲宗之幼也，太宗甚重之。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was young, Taizong held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke was still a boy, Ögedei favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 一日行幸，天大風，入帳殿，命憲宗坐膝下，撫其首曰：「是可以君天下。」

translations.literal: One day on an imperial outing the wind blew fiercely; entering the tent palace he seated Xianzong on his knees, stroked his head, and said: "This one can rule the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Once, caught in a gale on the road, Ögedei took shelter in his tent, set young Möngke on his knee, stroked the boy's head, and said, "This child can one day rule the world."

sentences.zh: 他日，用牸按豹，皇孫失烈門尚幼，曰：「以牸按豹，則犢將安所養？」

translations.literal: Another day, using a female leopard to pin down the quarry, the imperial grandson Shiremün, still young, said: "If a female leopard is used to hold down the leopard, where will the cub be nursed?"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Ögedei had a huntress leopard used to pin a quarry; Shiremün, still small, asked, "If you hold the mother down, who will suckle her cubs?"

sentences.zh: 太宗以為有仁心，又曰：「是可以君天下。」

translations.literal: Taizong thought this showed a benevolent heart and again said: "This one can rule the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei took this as proof of a compassionate heart and again declared, "This child can rule the world."

sentences.zh: 其後太宗崩，六皇后攝政，竟立定宗。

translations.literal: Afterward Taizong died; the Sixth Empress Dowager acted as regent and in the end enthroned Dingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after Ögedei's death the Sixth Empress Dowager seized power and enthroned Dingzong instead.

sentences.zh: 故至是，二人各舉以為言云。

translations.literal: Therefore at this time the two men each cited these words in their arguments, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: That is why each side now invoked Ögedei's words in support of its candidate.

sentences.zh: 憲宗既立，察哈臺之子及按赤臺等謀作亂，刳車轅，藏兵其中以入，轅折兵見，克薛傑見之，上變。

translations.literal: Once Xianzong was enthroned, the sons of Chagatai and Alchidei and others plotted rebellion; they hollowed chariot shafts and hid weapons within to bring inside; when a shaft broke the weapons were exposed; Keshijie saw this and reported the treachery.
translations.idiomatic: After Möngke's accession, Chagatai's faction and Alchidei conspired rebellion, smuggling weapons into the council inside hollowed wagon poles; when one pole snapped and the blades fell out, Keshijie witnessed it and raised the alarm.

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒即發兵迎之。

translations.literal: Manggesaer immediately dispatched troops to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Manggesaer at once marched out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 按赤臺不虞事遽覺，倉卒不能戰，遂悉就擒。

translations.literal: Alchidei did not expect the affair to be exposed so suddenly; in haste they could not fight, and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Caught unprepared, Alchidei's party could not mount a fight and was taken entire.

sentences.zh: 憲宗親簡其有罪者，付之鞫治。

translations.literal: Xianzong personally selected those who were guilty and handed them over to Manggesaer for interrogation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke personally marked out the guilty and handed them over for trial.

sentences.zh: 忙哥撒兒悉誅之。

translations.literal: Manggesaer executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Manggesaer had every one of them put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝以其奉法不阿，委任益專。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because he upheld the law without favoritism, entrusted him with ever more exclusive authority.
translations.idiomatic: Because he enforced the law without partiality, the emperor relied on him more absolutely than ever.

sentences.zh: 有當刑者，輒以法刑之，乃入奏，帝無不報可。

translations.literal: When someone deserved punishment he would punish according to law, then enter to report; the Emperor never failed to approve.
translations.idiomatic: He executed sentence first and reported afterward—and the emperor never once refused his judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝或臥未起，忙哥撒兒入奏事，至帳前，扣箭房，帝問何言，即可其奏，以所禦大帳行扇賜之。

translations.literal: Sometimes the Emperor had not yet risen from bed when Manggesaer entered to report business; arriving before the tent he knocked on the quiver-case; the Emperor asked what he wished to say and immediately approved his memorial, bestowing upon him the great tent's ceremonial fan the Emperor used when traveling.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the emperor had not yet risen, Manggesaer would come to the tent door, tap the quiver rack for admittance, state his business, receive instant approval, and be rewarded with the imperial processional fan from the great tent.

sentences.zh: 其見親寵如此。

translations.literal: Such was the intimacy and favor he enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the confidence and favor he commanded.

sentences.zh: 癸丑冬，病酒而卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the guichou year he died from illness caused by drink.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of guichou, broken by illness brought on by drink.

sentences.zh: 帝以忙哥撒兒當國時，多所誅戮，及是，咸騰謗言，乃為詔諭其子，略曰：

translations.literal: Because during Manggesaer's tenure of state affairs he had put many to death, by this time slander flourished everywhere; the Emperor therefore issued an edict instructing his sons, which in summary said:
translations.idiomatic: Manggesaer's stern justice had made him many enemies, and after his death slander ran wild; the emperor therefore addressed an edict to his sons, in substance as follows:

sentences.zh: 汝高祖赤老溫愷赤暨汝祖搠阿，事我成吉思皇帝，皆著勞績，惟朕皇祖實褒嘉之。

translations.literal: Your great-grandfather Chilaun Qiqi and your grandfather Shuo'a served my Genghis Emperor and both rendered distinguished service; my imperial grandfather truly praised and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Your great-grandfather Chilaun Qiqi and your grandfather Shuo'a served Genghis Khan with conspicuous merit, and my imperial grandfather honored them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 汝父忙哥撒兒，自其幼時，事我太宗，朝夕忠勤，罔有過咎。

translations.literal: Your father Manggesaer, from his youth, served my Taizong with loyal diligence morning and evening, without fault or blame.
translations.idiomatic: Your father Manggesaer served Ögedei from boyhood with unwavering loyalty day and night, and never once fell short.

sentences.zh: 從我皇考，經營四方。

translations.literal: Following my imperial father, he managed affairs in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He followed my father Tolui in the conquest of the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 迨事皇妣及朕兄弟，亦罔有過咎。

translations.literal: When he came to serve my imperial mother and us brothers, likewise there was no fault or blame.
translations.idiomatic: In service to my mother and to us brothers he was equally beyond reproach.

sentences.zh: 暨朕討定斡羅思、阿速、穩兒別裏欽察之域，濟大川，造方舟，伐山通道，攻城野戰，功多於諸將。

translations.literal: When I subdued Rus, the Alans, the Cumans of the Ural region, crossed great rivers, built many boats, cut through mountains to open roads, stormed cities and fought in the field, his merit exceeded that of the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In my campaigns against Rus, the Alans, and the Urals Cumans—in crossing great rivers, building fleets, cutting roads through mountains, besieging cities and fighting in the open field—he outstripped every other commander.

sentences.zh: 俘厥寶玉，大賚諸將，則退然無欲得之心。

translations.literal: When captured jewels were lavishly bestowed on the generals, he modestly had no desire to obtain any.
translations.idiomatic: When plunder was divided among the generals he alone showed no eagerness to take his share.

sentences.zh: 惟朕言是用，修我邦憲，治我蒐田，輯我國家，罔不咸乂。

translations.literal: He used only my words as guide, repaired our state's laws, administered our hunting grounds, put our nation in order—in nothing was there disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out my word alone—reforming the laws, governing the hunt, putting the realm in order—until nothing was left unsettled.

sentences.zh: 惟厥忠，雖其私親，與朕嬪御，小有過咎，一是無有比私。

translations.literal: In his loyalty alone, even toward his own kin and my consorts, when there were minor faults he showed no partiality whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: So loyal was he that when even his own relatives—or my consorts—erred in small matters, he showed them no favor.

sentences.zh: 故朕皇妣，迨朕昆弟，無不嘉賴。

translations.literal: Therefore my imperial mother, down to us brothers, all relied on him with approval.
translations.idiomatic: My mother and all of us brothers came to depend on him and praise his service.

sentences.zh: 朝之老臣、宿衛耆舊，無不嚴畏。

translations.literal: The old ministers of the court and the elder veterans of the guard—all without exception stood in strict awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran ministers and the old guard alike stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 錄其勤勞，命為劄魯忽赤，治朕皇考受民，布昭大公，以辨獄慎民，爰作朕股肱耳目，眾無嘩言，朕聽以安。

translations.literal: Recording his labor and merit, I appointed him jarquchi to govern the people my imperial father had received, proclaiming great fairness, to distinguish cases and treat the people with care; he became my arms, legs, eyes, and ears—the crowd had no clamor, and my hearing was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In reward for his service I made him chief jarquchi over the subjects my father had entrusted to the throne—proclaiming impartial justice, deciding cases, and guarding the people. He became my hands, my eyes, my ears; the court fell silent, and I governed in peace.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，察哈臺阿哈之孫，太宗之裔定宗、闊出之子，及其民人，越有他誌。

translations.literal: From that time onward, the grandson of Chagatai Aqa, the descendants of Taizong Dingzong and Kuo-chu's sons, and their people all turned to other designs.
translations.idiomatic: After that, Chagatai's grandson, Ögedei's line through Dingzong and Kuo-chu's sons, and their followers all turned against the throne.

sentences.zh: 賴天之靈，時則有克薛傑者，以告於朕。

translations.literal: Relying on Heaven's spirit, at that time there was Keshijie, who reported to me.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent Keshijie to bring me word of their plot.

sentences.zh: 汝父肅將大旅，以遏亂略，按赤臺等謀是用潰，悉就拘執。

translations.literal: Your father solemnly led a great host to check the chaos and rapine; through Alchidei's and the others' conspiracy being thus shattered, all were taken and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Your father marched at the head of a great force to crush the rebellion; Alchidei's conspiracy collapsed, and the plotters were seized.

sentences.zh: 朕取有罪者，使辨治之，汝父體朕之公，其刑其宥，克比於法。

translations.literal: I took those who were guilty and had them tried and judged; your father embodied my fairness—in punishment and in pardon he measured up to the law.
translations.idiomatic: I singled out the guilty for trial; your father embodied my justice, meting out punishment and mercy according to the law.

sentences.zh: 又使治也速、不裏獄，亦克比於法。

translations.literal: I also had him judge the cases of Yesü and Buri, and there too he measured up to the law.
translations.idiomatic: He tried the cases of Yesü and Buri with the same fidelity to law.

sentences.zh: 惟爾脫歡、脫兒赤：自朕用汝父，用法不阿，兄弟親姻，咸麗於憲。

translations.literal: As for you, Tuohuan and Tuo'erchi: since I employed your father, he applied the law without favoritism; brothers and kinsmen by marriage all felt the weight of the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: To you, Tuohuan and Tuo'erchi: from the day I put your father in office he showed no favor in judgment—brothers and in-laws alike fell under the law.

sentences.zh: 今眾罔不怨，曰「爾亦有死耶」，若有慊誌。

translations.literal: Now the multitude all grumble without exception, saying "Will you too die?"—as if nursing grievance in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Now the mob mutters everywhere, "Will you die too?"—as though the executions had been personal vendettas.

sentences.zh: 人則雖死，朕將寵之如生。

translations.literal: Though the man is dead, I shall cherish him as if he lived.
translations.idiomatic: Though your father is gone, I shall honor him as though he still lived.

sentences.zh: 肆朕訓汝，爾克明時朕言，如是而有福，不如是而有禍。

translations.literal: Therefore I instruct you: if you can illumine and heed my words, by doing so there will be blessing; by not doing so there will be calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Hear my counsel: heed these words and fortune will follow; defy them and ruin will come.

sentences.zh: 惟天惟君，能禍福人；

translations.literal: Only Heaven and only the sovereign can bless or afflict men;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven alone and the throne alone can raise a man up or cast him down;

sentences.zh: 惟天惟君，是敬是畏。

translations.literal: only Heaven and only the sovereign are to be reverenced and feared.
translations.idiomatic: therefore fear Heaven and fear your sovereign.

sentences.zh: 立身正直，制行貞潔，是汝之福；

translations.literal: To stand upright in person and govern conduct with purity—that is your blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Upright conduct and a clean life are your protection;

sentences.zh: 反是勿思也。

translations.literal: do not consider the opposite.
translations.idiomatic: do not even entertain the alternative.

sentences.zh: 能用朕言，則不墜汝父之道，人亦不能間汝矣；

translations.literal: If you can use my words, you will not let your father's way fall; others likewise cannot sow division against you;
translations.idiomatic: Follow my word and you will uphold your father's legacy, and no man will be able to turn the court against you;

sentences.zh: 不用朕言，則人將仇汝、伺汝、間汝。

translations.literal: if you do not use my words, then men will hate you, watch you, and set you at odds with others.
translations.idiomatic: reject it, and men will hate you, spy on you, and work to destroy you.

sentences.zh: 怨汝父者，必曰「汝亦與我夷矣」，汝則殆哉。

translations.literal: Those who resent your father will surely say, "You too shall be destroyed with me," and then you will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hated your father will say, "You shall be destroyed along with me," and you will be in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 汝於朕言，弗慎繹之，汝則有咎；

translations.literal: If you do not carefully ponder my words, you will be at fault;
translations.idiomatic: If you do not weigh my words carefully, you will bring blame upon yourself;

sentences.zh: 克慎繹之，人將敬汝畏汝，無間伺汝，無慢汝怨汝者矣。

translations.literal: if you can ponder them carefully, people will respect and fear you, none will spy on you, and none will slight or resent you.
translations.idiomatic: but if you heed them well, people will honor and fear you, none will find occasion against you, and none will despise or hate you.

sentences.zh: 又，而母而婦，有讒欺巧佞構亂之言，慎勿聽之，則盡善矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, whether from your mother or your wife, if there are words of slander, deceit, cunning flattery, or stirring up trouble, take care not to heed them—then all will be well.
translations.idiomatic: And whether from your mother or your wife, beware of slander, deceit, and cunning words meant to sow discord—refuse to listen, and all will be well.

sentences.zh: 至順四年，追封忙哥撒兒為兗國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhishun, Manggesaer was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhishun, Manggesaer was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 子四人：長脫歡，次脫兒赤，次也先帖木爾，次帖木兒不花。

translations.literal: He had four sons: the eldest Tuohuan, next Tuoerchi, next Yesiantiemuer, and next Temuerbuhua.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Tuohuan, Tuoerchi, Yesiantiemuer, and Temuerbuhua.

sentences.zh: 脫歡為萬戶，無子。

translations.literal: Tuohuan was a myriarch and had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Tuohuan held the rank of myriarch and left no sons.

sentences.zh: 脫兒赤子明禮帖木兒，累官翰林學士承旨，從征乃顏有功。

translations.literal: Tuoerchi's son Minglitiemuer rose through repeated appointments to Hanlin Academician Expositor and performed meritorious service in the campaign against Nayan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoerchi's son Minglitiemuer rose to Hanlin Academician Expositor and distinguished himself in the campaign against Nayan.

sentences.zh: 明禮帖木兒子咬住，咬住子也先，延徽寺卿。

translations.literal: Minglitiemuer's son Yaozhu; Yaozhu's son Yexian, Director of the Yanhui Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Minglitiemuer's son was Yaozhu; Yaozhu's son Yexian became Director of the Yanhui Temple.

sentences.zh: 也先帖木兒子曰哈剌合孫。

translations.literal: Yesiantiemuer's son was Halahesun.
translations.idiomatic: Yesiantiemuer's son was Halahesun.

sentences.zh: 帖木兒不花子曰塔術納，曰哈裏哈孫，曰伯答沙。

translations.literal: Temuerbuhua's sons were Tashuna, Halihasun, and Bodasha.
translations.idiomatic: Temuerbuhua's sons were Tashuna, Halihasun, and Bodasha.

sentences.zh: 伯答沙為人清慎寬厚，號稱長者。

translations.literal: Bodasha was pure, cautious, and generous in character, and was known as an elder of worth.
translations.idiomatic: Bodasha was upright, prudent, and magnanimous, and was known as a man of exemplary character.

sentences.zh: 其歿也，貧無以為斂，人皆嘆其廉。

translations.literal: When he died he was too poor to afford burial, and all lamented his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was too poor even to afford a proper burial, and all praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 詔贈推忠佐理正德秉義功臣、開府儀同三司、太師、上柱國，追封威平王。

translations.literal: An edict granted him Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty and Assists Governance with Upright Virtue and Righteous Conduct, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ceremonial Parity with the Three Excellencies, Grand Preceptor, and Upper Pillar of the State; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Weiping.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was honored as Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty and Assists Governance with Upright Virtue and Righteous Conduct, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Master with Ceremonial Parity with the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Weiping.

sentences.zh: 三子：長馬馬的斤，次潑皮，次八郎。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Mamadejin, next Popi, and next Balang.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Mamadejin, Popi, and Balang.

sentences.zh: 八郎期而孤，其母乞咬契氏二十而寡，守節不他適。

translations.literal: Balang was orphaned while still young; his mother Lady Qiyaoqi was widowed at twenty and preserved her chastity without remarrying.
translations.idiomatic: Balang lost his father while still a boy; his mother Lady Qiyaoqi was widowed at twenty and remained faithful without taking another husband.

sentences.zh: 八郎後為大宗正府劄魯忽赤，能繼其先。

translations.literal: Balang later became Jarquchi of the Grand Council for Princes and was able to carry on his forebears' work.
translations.idiomatic: Balang later served as Jarquchi in the Grand Council for Princes and upheld his family's legacy.

sentences.zh: 有成立者，母氏之教也。

translations.literal: That he achieved success was due to his mother's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His success was owed to his mother's teaching.

sentences.zh: 孟速思

translations.literal: Mengsusi
translations.idiomatic: Mengsusi

sentences.zh: 孟速思，畏兀人，世居別失八里，古北庭都護之地。

translations.literal: Mengsusi was a man of the Uyghurs, whose family had long dwelt at Bieshibali, the ancient seat of the Protectorate of Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsusi was an Uyghur whose family had long lived at Bieshibali, site of the ancient Protectorate of Beiting.

sentences.zh: 幼有奇質，年十五，盡通本國書。

translations.literal: From youth he showed extraordinary gifts; by age fifteen he had fully mastered his native script.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he showed exceptional talent; by fifteen he had mastered the Uyghur script completely.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，召至闕下，一見大悅，曰：「此兒目中有火，它日可大用。」

translations.literal: Taizu heard of him and summoned him to court; at first sight he was greatly pleased and said: "This boy has fire in his eyes; one day he will be of great use."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu heard of him he summoned him to court and was delighted at first sight. "This boy has fire in his eyes," he said; "one day he will serve in great matters."

sentences.zh: 以授睿宗，使視顯懿莊聖皇后分邑歲賦。

translations.literal: He gave him to Ruizong to oversee the annual revenues of the estates allotted to Empress Xianyi Zhuangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: He placed him in Ruizong's service to supervise the annual revenues of Empress Xianyi Zhuangsheng's allotted estates.

sentences.zh: 復事世祖於潛藩，日見親用。

translations.literal: He again served Shizu in his princely residence and daily grew in favor and employment.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Shizu when the latter was still heir apparent, and day by day won greater trust.

sentences.zh: 憲宗崩，孟速思言於世祖曰：「神器不可久曠，太祖嫡孫，唯王最長且賢，宜即皇帝位。」

translations.literal: When Xianzong died, Mengsusi said to Shizu: "The imperial regalia cannot long lie vacant; among Taizu's legitimate grandsons, Your Highness alone is eldest and worthy—you ought to take the throne at once."
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong died, Mengsusi urged Shizu: "The throne cannot remain empty. Among Taizu's legitimate grandsons, you alone are eldest and most worthy—you should take the throne without delay."

sentences.zh: 諸王塔察兒、也孫哥、合丹等，咸是其言。

translations.literal: The princes Qachar, Yesunge, and Hedan, among others, all endorsed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Qachar, Yesunge, Hedan, and others all agreed.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，眷顧益重。

translations.literal: When Shizu acceded to the throne, his favor and regard grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu took the throne his favor toward Mengsusi only deepened.

sentences.zh: 南征時，與近臣不只兒為斷事官。

translations.literal: During the southern campaign he served with the intimate attendant Buzhier as judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign he served alongside the intimate attendant Buzhier as judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 及諸王阿裏不哥叛，相拒漠北，不只兒有二心，孟速思知之，奏徙之於中都，親監護以往，帝以為忠。

translations.literal: When Prince Alibuge rebelled and the two sides confronted each other in the northern deserts, Buzhier harbored divided loyalties; Mengsusi learned of this, memorialized to transfer him to Zhongdu, and personally escorted him there—the emperor regarded this as loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Alibuge rebelled and the court faced him in the northern steppe, Mengsusi discovered that Buzhier was wavering in his loyalty. He memorialized to move Buzhier to Zhongdu and personally escorted him there; the emperor took this as proof of Mengsusi's fidelity.

sentences.zh: 數命收召豪俊，凡所引薦，皆極其選。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly ordered to gather outstanding men; every person he recommended was of the highest caliber.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly charged with recruiting talented men, and every candidate he recommended was of the finest quality.

sentences.zh: 詔與安童並拜丞相，固辭。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Grand Councillor jointly with Antong, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as Grand Councillor alongside Antong but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝語安童及丞相伯顏、御史大夫月魯那演等曰：「賢哉孟速思，求之彼族，誠為罕也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Antong, Grand Councillor Bayan, Censor-in-Chief Yuelunayan, and others: "How worthy is Mengsusi! To find such a man among that people is truly rare."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Antong, Grand Councillor Bayan, Censor-in-Chief Yuelunayan, and the others: "Mengsusi is a man of rare merit—among his people such talent is hard to find."

sentences.zh: 孟速思為人剛嚴謹信。

translations.literal: Mengsusi was by nature stern, strict, and trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsusi was stern, rigorous, and utterly trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 蚤居帷幄，謀議世莫得聞。

translations.literal: From early on he dwelt within the command tent, and the world never heard his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Long before he had served within the command tent, yet his counsel never reached the outside world.

sentences.zh: 至元四年卒，年六十有二。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhiyuan, at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Zhiyuan era, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝尤哀悼，特謚敏惠。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply and specially granted the posthumous name Minhui (Keen and Gracious).
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and granted the posthumous name Minhui, Keen and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 武宗朝，贈推忠同德佐理功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封武都王，改謚智敏。

translations.literal: Under Wuzong he was posthumously granted Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty and Joint Virtue in Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ceremonial Parity with the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Prince of Wudu with the name changed to Zhimin (Wise and Keen).
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong he was posthumously honored as Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty and Joint Virtue in Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Master with Ceremonial Parity with the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Prince of Wudu with the temple name changed to Zhimin, Wise and Keen.

sentences.zh: 子九人，多至大官。

translations.literal: He had nine sons, many of whom rose to high office.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons, many of whom attained high rank.
